Definition: The country's total international internet bandwidth capacity per internet user, indicating the quality and capacity of the country's connection to the global internet. Determined by submarine cable landings (for coastal states), cross-border terrestrial fibre (for landlocked states), and satellite links.
revision_notes: Original ITU 2017 country profile PDF could not be fetched directly (request blocked) but its 2016 figure is corroborated by TheGlobalEconomy.com (4.32 kbit/s per user, citing ITU) and Research ICT Africa's State of ICT in Lesotho report (3.86 kbit/s per user, ITU 2016). No newer ITU international-bandwidth-per-user figure for Lesotho was found; the ITU's 2019 IDI presentation lists Lesotho as not available for this indicator. Score of 1 (Very Low, <5 kbit/s) confirmed against the metadata scale.
revised_comments: Lesotho's international internet bandwidth stood at approximately 4.3 kbit/s per internet user in 2016, the most recent year for which ITU data is available, reflecting very low international connectivity capacity relative to the African regional average (around 31 kbit/s per user) and the global average (over 150 kbit/s per user).

Definition: The number and activity level of technology hubs, incubators, accelerators, and co-working spaces focused on technology and innovation. These provide physical infrastructure and support for tech entrepreneurship and skills development.
Comments: None listed in AfriLabs/Briter Bridges reports
revision_notes: Original score of 1 (None identified) rested on the 2019 AfriLabs/Briter Bridges 100-hub report, which did not list any Lesotho hub. Current evidence, fetched and read directly from source, shows at least four active hubs with regular activity: the NUL Innovation Hub at the National University of Lesotho (established 2018, over 50 start-ups incubated), the government's AfriLabs-listed Lesotho Entrepreneurship Hub & Seed Financing Facility (World Bank/CAFI-funded, incubating cohorts of 50 enterprises through to 2028), Limkokwing University's Entrepreneurship Accelerator Hub, and Vodacom Lesotho's Software Factory Hub (launched in Maseru, 2024). This meets the '3-9 hubs with regular activity' band on the metadata scale. Score revised upward to 3; not a top-of-scale promotion so standard confirmation applies.
revised_comments: Lesotho hosts several active technology and innovation hubs with regular programming. These include the National University of Lesotho's Innovation Hub in Roma, established in 2018, which has incubated more than 50 start-ups and created over 500 jobs; the government-backed Lesotho Entrepreneurship Hub & Seed Financing Facility, supported by a World Bank-funded CAFI project targeting 500 incubated enterprises by 2028; Limkokwing University's Entrepreneurship Accelerator Hub, which has incubated ICT and other ventures; and Vodacom Lesotho's Software Factory Hub, a incubation programme for local tech start-ups launched in Maseru in 2024.

Definition: The scale and quality of tertiary-level ICT and STEM education programmes available in the country, based on the number and quality of institutions offering ICT degrees, computer science programmes, and engineering courses relative to the population.
Value Name: Very limited (<2 institutions with ICT programmes)
Comments: Very limited institutions, low TVET budget
revision_notes: Original score of 1 (Very limited, <2 institutions with ICT programmes) was based on the 2022 UN Technology Bank Technology Needs Assessment report's general assessment of limited STI capacity and low TVET budget, which did not enumerate specific institutions offering ICT degrees. Direct verification of institution websites and Lesotho's Council on Higher Education accreditation register identifies at least three tertiary institutions with active, accredited ICT programmes: the National University of Lesotho (BSc Computer Science, BSc Information Systems, BEng Computer Systems and Networks, BEng Electronics), Limkokwing University of Creative Technology's Lesotho campus (Faculty of Information Technology: Software Engineering with Multimedia, E-commerce, Business Information Technology), and Botho University's Lesotho campus (BSc Computing, Computer Networking, Data Science, Mobile Computing, all CHE-accredited through 2024-2030). This meets the 'several institutions, growing enrolment' band on the metadata scale. Score revised upward to 3; not a top-of-scale promotion.
revised_comments: Lesotho has several tertiary institutions offering ICT and STEM degree programmes with growing enrolment. The National University of Lesotho's Faculty of Science and Technology offers BSc degrees in Computer Science, Information Systems and Electronics alongside BEng degrees in Computer Systems and Networks and Electronics. Limkokwing University of Creative Technology's Lesotho campus runs a Faculty of Information Technology offering Software Engineering with Multimedia, E-commerce and Business Information Technology degrees. Botho University's Lesotho campus, accredited by Lesotho's Council on Higher Education, offers BSc programmes in Computing, Computer Networking, Data Science and Mobile Computing.
